en: Experience Blitzy firsthand at blitzy.com slash twiml.

en: So far, most of the biggest breakthroughs in AI have come from training larger models on even more data.
zh: 迄今为止，AI 中最大的突破大部分来自于在更多数据上训练更大的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's not the only way forward.
zh: 但这并非唯一的出路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today's guest, Max Welling, believes that better AI may come from someplace very different, physics.
zh: 今天的嘉宾 Max Welling 认为，更好的 AI 可能来自一个非常不同的地方，物理学。

speaker: Unknown
en: Max is the co-founder and CTO of cusp.ai and a professor at the University of Amsterdam.
zh: Max 是 cusp.ai 的联合创始人和 CTO，也是阿姆斯特丹大学的教授。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 在 cusp.ai，他的团队正在使用生成式 AI 为半导体、电池、碳捕获和其他科学应用设计全新的材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: But our conversation goes beyond AI for science.
zh: 但我们的对话超越了科学领域的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Max argues that physics isn't just another domain where AI can be applied.
zh: Max 认为，物理学不仅仅是 AI 可以应用的另一个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: The mathematical ideas physicists have developed to understand the natural world, concepts like thermodynamics, wave propagation, and symmetry breaking, may also help shape the next generation of AI architectures.
zh: 物理学家为了理解自然界而发展出的数学思想，如热力学、波的传播和对称性破缺等概念，可能也有助于塑造下一代 AI 架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's Max on why physics may shape the next generation of AI.
zh: 这里是 Max 关于为什么物理学可能会塑造下一代 AI 的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Waves are actually seen in the brain now because we've gone from single electrode measurements to maybe hundreds or thousands of electrode measurements.
zh: 现在实际上在大脑中看到了波，因为我们已经从单电极测量变成了可能数百或数千个电极测量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, in a single electrode, you cannot see a moving wave, a traveling wave.
zh: 当然，在单个电极中，你无法看到移动的波，行进的波。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you put hundreds or thousands in them, you can actually see these traveling waves and people have now observed them everywhere.
zh: 但是如果你把数百或数千个（电极）放进去，你实际上可以看到这些行进波，人们现在已经到处观察到它们了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In neural networks, it's always been a little hard.
zh: 在神经网络中，一直有点困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: To make sure that the information travels all the way from the input to the output layers through thousands of layers.
zh: 确保信息通过数千层从输入层一直传输到输出层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the question becomes, how do you communicate very deep into time or reason very deep into time?
zh: 所以问题变成了，你如何在时间上通信得很深或在时间上推理得很深？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or how do you communicate with things that are very far away in your brain?
zh: 或者你如何与你大脑中非常遥远的事物进行通信？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question becomes, can we actually start using this phenomenon?
zh: 所以问题变成了，我们实际上能开始使用这种现象吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This wave phenomenon that we see in the brain, can we also start to use it in neural networks?
zh: 我们在大脑中看到的这种波现象，我们是否也可以开始在神经网络中使用它？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this has been the work that we've been developing.
zh: 因此这就是我们一直在开发的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Sam Charrington, and this is the TwiML AI Podcast.
zh: 我是 Sam Charrington，这是 TwiML AI 播客。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 十多年来，我通过像这样的对话一直在探索塑造 AI 未来的想法和创新，这些对话帮助你理解什么是真实的，什么是下一个，什么是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's jump in.
zh: 让我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Max, it's so great to be on the line with you again.
zh: Max，能再次和你通电话真是太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a while.
zh: 有一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great to be back, Sam.
zh: 很高兴回来，Sam。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm looking forward to our discussion.
zh: 我期待我们的讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am as well.
zh: 我也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our audience can look up our conversations from, I think, 2019 and 2020.
zh: 我们的听众可以查找我们在，我想，2019 年和 2020 年的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: where we covered what you were working on at the time and I think still echoes into your work today.
zh: 在那些对话中我们涵盖了当时你在做什么，我认为这至今仍回响在你的工作中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Geometric neural networks and gauge equivariance neural networks and the like.
zh: 几何神经网络和规范等变神经网络之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'd love to have you kind of catch us up on what you've been up to since.
zh: 但我想让你给我们大致补补课，讲讲你从那以后一直在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been quite a while.
zh: 确实有一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, actually, the equivariance theme has definitely continued.
zh: 是的，实际上，等变主题肯定在继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, I found out that equivariance was used very fruitfully in chemistry and material science.
zh: 事实上，我发现等变在化学和材料科学中被非常富有成效地使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in chemistry and material science, people train neural network models to predict the forces on atoms because people want to evolve atoms forward in time in order to compute their properties, which is called molecular dynamics.
zh: 所以在化学和材料科学中，人们训练神经网络模型来预测原子上的力，因为人们想让原子随时间向前演化以计算它们的属性，这被称为分子动力学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And typically you need to use quantum mechanics to compute these forces because a large contribution comes from the electrons and electrons are very light.
zh: 而且通常你需要使用量子力学来计算这些力，因为很大一部分贡献来自电子，而且电子非常轻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need to treat them with quantum mechanics.
zh: 所以你需要用量子力学来处理它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, if you get 10 electrons or more, it basically becomes completely unfeasible to solve the so-called Schrodinger equation.
zh: 但是，你知道，如果你有 10 个或更多电子，基本上完全不可行去求解所谓的薛定谔方程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people have come up with approximations like density functional theory, known as DFT.
zh: 所以人们提出了像密度泛函理论这样的近似方法，即 DFT。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the inventors of that got the Nobel Prize for that.
zh: 而且那的发明者因此获得了诺贝尔奖。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what now people do is they train surrogates.
zh: 但是现在人们做的是他们训练替代模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they provide data using this expensive approximation to quantum mechanics.
zh: 所以他们提供数据，使用这种昂贵的量子力学近似。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they use neural networks to shortcut the computation, so to predict the outcome of that computation, but at a much more accelerated pace.
zh: 然后他们使用神经网络来抄近道计算，以便预测该计算的结果，但是以一个更快的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in other words,
zh: 换句话说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Three-order to four-order magnitude acceleration, more efficiency relative to these quantum mechanical approximations.
zh: 三到四个数量级的加速，相对于这些量子力学近似更有效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in those models, because the world is three-dimensional symmetric, so if I rotate a molecule, all the forces will rotate with it, and so we could now put the same ideas that we use for images, we could put them in these molecules, these models that predict the forces.
zh: 而在那些模型中，因为世界是三维对称的，所以如果我旋转一个分子，所有的力都会随之旋转，所以我们可以现在把同样的想法，就是我们用于图像的，我们可以把它们放入这些分子中，这些预测力的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we could use equivariance.
zh: 我们可以使用等变性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why I kind of, also because my background is in science.
zh: 这就是为什么我有点，也因为我的背景是在科学。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did my PhD in theoretical physics.
zh: 我在理论物理方面读的博士。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought, okay, this is a perfect unification of my old sort of passion and my new passion.
zh: 我想，好吧，这是我旧的那种热情和我新热情的完美结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can put it together.
zh: 我可以把它们结合起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's when I started to be interested in AI for science.
zh: 那就是我开始对用于科学的 AI 感兴趣的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that led pretty directly to the founding of CUSP.
zh: 所以这相当直接地导致了 CUSP 的成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, first, I spent two years at Microsoft Research as a VP because they were building their AFR science lab in Amsterdam, and so I helped that along.
zh: 实际上，首先，我在微软研究院花了两年时间做副总裁，因为他们在阿姆斯特丹建立他们的 AFR 科学实验室，所以我帮助推进了那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But after two years, I wanted to start a startup.
zh: 但两年后，我想开始一家初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I already did a startup a while ago, but this was actually the startup that got acquired by Qualcomm, and then I spent some time at Qualcomm.
zh: 我之前做过一家初创公司，但这实际上是那家被高通收购的初创公司，然后我在高通花了一些时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really like startups, the dynamical environment and the impact you can make.
zh: 我真的很喜欢初创公司，那种动态的环境和你能产生的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted to do it the Silicon Valley way together with my co-founder, Chad Edwards.
zh: 我想用硅谷的方式来做，和我的联合创始人 Chad Edwards 一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we started Cospy AI in 2024.
zh: 所以我们在 2024 年创立了 Cospy AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk a little bit about the progress that you've made since then.
zh: 稍微谈谈从那时起你们取得的进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the kind of shape of the company today?
zh: 今天公司的大致情况是什么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a huge ride, actually.
zh: 这实际上是一段巨大的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a roller coaster.
zh: 这就像过山车。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started, I think, about two years ago.
zh: 所以我们在，我想，大约两年前开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, May, spring 24.
zh: 所以，你知道，五月，2024 年春天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we started with a good initial investment of about 30 million, from which we could hire an excellent team.
zh: 是的，我们以大约 3000 万的良好初始投资开始，从中我们可以聘请一个优秀的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the team has grown to about 50 people right now.
zh: 所以团队现在已经增长到大约 50 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We now also have labs in London and Berlin.
zh: 我们现在在伦敦和柏林也有实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're also expanding into Asia and North America.
zh: 我们也在向亚洲和北美扩张。

speaker: Unknown
en: And no surprise, your list of advisors is a bit of a who's who with Jeff Hinton and Jan LeCun at the top of the list.
zh: 毫不奇怪，你的顾问名单有点像名人录，Jeff Hinton 和 Jan LeCun 名列榜首。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, the advisors are actually fantastic.
zh: 是的，顾问们实际上非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have Jeff Hinton and Jan LeCun.
zh: 所以我们有 Jeff Hinton 和 Jan LeCun。

speaker: Unknown
en: We added to that also Martin van den Brink.
zh: 我们还增加了 Martin van den Brink。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Laura Brown.
zh: 以及 Laura Brown。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Laura Brown is the former CEO of BP.
zh: 所以 Laura Brown 是 BP 的前 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Martin van den Brink is the former president and CTO of ASML.
zh: 而 Martin van den Brink 是 ASML 的前总裁兼 CTO。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're both retired, and they like to spend their time with new startups and help them along.
zh: 他们都退休了，他们喜欢把时间花在新的初创公司上并帮助它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's Verity Harding.
zh: 然后还有 Verity Harding。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's working for the UK government and also DeepMind, I think, or maybe formerly at DeepMind.
zh: 她在为英国政府工作，也在 DeepMind，我想，或者可能以前在 DeepMind。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Kristin Persson, who has sort of initiated the materials project, and she's also advising on that side.
zh: 然后还有 Kristin Persson，她发起了 materials project，她也在那方面提供建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got it.
zh: 明白了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's dig into the technology and the approach that you're taking to kind of apply this original set of work that you developed to materials.
zh: 所以让我们深入研究一下你正在采取的技术和方法，以某种方式将你开发的这套原始工作应用到材料上。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you get started with that effort?
zh: 你是如何开始这项工作的？

speaker: Unknown
en: The opportunity is, to me, there's a deep fascination with the fact that there is a sheer infinite amount of possibilities in which you can put together atoms.
zh: 这个机会在于，对我来说，深深着迷于这样一个事实，即你可以将原子组合在一起的方式有着纯粹无限的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the universe has only figured out so many of them because they form naturally, I guess, in the universe.
zh: 而宇宙只弄清楚了其中这么多，因为它们在宇宙中自然形成，我猜。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's many more that you can design yourself with all sorts of exotic properties.
zh: 但还有更多你可以自己设计的，具有各种奇异的特性。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we started this company, both Chad and I were
zh: 当我们创办这家公司时，Chad 和我都

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm kind of concerned about the climate.
zh: 我有点担心气候。

speaker: Unknown
en: We still are.
zh: 我们仍然如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we felt there's a strong need to accelerate the energy transition to more sustainable energy sources, as well as trying to take the carbon dioxide that's in the atmosphere out.
zh: 所以我们感到强烈需要加速能源转型，转向更可持续的能源，以及尝试把大气中的二氧化碳抽取出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So not many people know that by the time it's 2015, of course, we really like to be completely carbon neutral.
zh: 所以没多少人知道，到了 2015 年，当然，我们真的很想完全实现碳中和。

speaker: Unknown
en: But after that, there is still 50 to 100 years where we have to take out every year about half of what we currently put in.
zh: 但在那之后，仍有 50 到 100 年的时间，我们需要每年提取出当前排放量的大约一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's 20 gigaton a year.
zh: 所以那就是每年 200 亿吨。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an enormous amount.
zh: 那是一个巨大的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the size of the Lake of Geneva filled with sort of liquid carbon dioxide, a gigantic amount.
zh: 我想就像是日内瓦湖那么大，装满了液态二氧化碳，一个巨大的数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't have the technology for that because it's actually very hard to take it out.
zh: 而且我们没有这项技术，因为实际上把它提取出来非常困难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because it's so dilute in the atmosphere, it's very expensive too.
zh: 因为它在大气中太稀薄了，所以也非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the two factors which are more expensive are energy and the material, the sorbit material that you use in order to take the carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere.
zh: 而其中更昂贵的两个因素是能源和材料，即你用来从大气中提取二氧化碳的 sorbit 材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we've been working, the first project we've been doing was improving the materials that take out this carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
zh: 所以我们一直在工作，我们做的第一个项目是改进这些从大气中提取二氧化碳的材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are called metal organic frameworks.
zh: 这些被称为金属有机框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, this is the material that this year won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
zh: 实际上，这是今年获得诺贝尔化学奖的材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, so we built a platform, and I can go into much more detail, but we built a platform that designs these material with the use of AI.
zh: 是的，所以我们构建了一个平台，我可以更详细地介绍，但我们构建了一个利用 AI 设计这些材料的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can sort of think of it as a search engine, but it's not searching over existing documents.
zh: 所以你可以把它看作是一个搜索引擎，但它不是在搜索现有的文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: It searches over known and unknown materials.
zh: 它搜索已知和未知的材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it actually completely designs them from scratch if there's no suitable ones already available.
zh: 所以如果没有现成的合适材料，它实际上会完全从头开始设计它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's many components.
zh: 并且有许多组件。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's agentic, so there is an agent sitting at the core of it who orchestrates a long computation.
zh: 它是智能体化的，所以有一个智能体坐在它的核心，它编排着一个长计算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it searches through existing databases.
zh: 它搜索现有的数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: It generates entirely new molecules.
zh: 它生成全新的分子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it also evaluates all these molecules with all sorts of tools.
zh: 它还用各种工具评估所有这些分子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in this generation and evaluation, you know, equivariance and all sorts of methods that, you know, we have developed over the years in my academic lab play a very important role.
zh: 在这个生成和评估过程中，你知道，equivariance 和我们在我的学术实验室多年来开发的各种方法起着非常重要的作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: To be clear, you mentioned a molecule that won the Nobel Prize.
zh: 说清楚点，你提到了一种获得诺贝尔奖的分子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you involved in the discovery of that particular molecule?
zh: 你参与了那个特定分子的发现吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I wish.
zh: 不，我希望是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those were chemists who did that, who discovered it.
zh: 那是完成这件事的化学家，是他们发现的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Professor Kitagawa, Professor Yagi, and Professor Robson, I think those are the three.
zh: 我想是 Kitagawa 教授、Yagi 教授和 Robson 教授，我想那是这三位。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not quite sure of the last one.
zh: 我不太确定最后一位。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is a class of molecules where there is a metal complex, a metal node with all sorts of atoms along it at the vertices of a graph.
zh: 但这是一类分子，其中有一个金属络合物，一个金属节点，沿着它有各种原子位于图的顶点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there is so-called linkers, which are also organic complexes, which are connecting these vertices on the graph.
zh: 然后有所谓的连接体，它们也是有机络合物，连接着图上的这些顶点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're extremely porous.
zh: 而且它们极其多孔。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they have a very large holes in the middle with an enormous surface area.
zh: 所以它们中间有很大的孔，具有巨大的表面积。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you blow sort of air atmosphere through it, the molecules in the air, which is water, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide, but carbon dioxide is only a small fraction of that, they tend to stick to the sides.
